inputs.root_cause: XLIFF-PRESERVE-001's two obligations were confirmed genuinely unbuilt in an earlier tick this session: dumps()/dump() had exactly one output path with no LOSSLESS-vs-CANONICAL caller choice, and no LossReport/check_preservation-style API existed anywhere in the package. The identical gap was independently confirmed in UBL's parallel obligation. This tick closed XLIFF's half with real production source.

execution_steps: 1. Read model/document.py and codec/writer/writer.py in full to find what this model already distinguishes as modeled vs unmodeled content. Found ExtensionNode (an explicit typed slot for 'an unknown or not-yet-typed namespaced XML subtree') attached at document/file/group/unit level, plus a separate extensions list on Segment -- the one place this model already draws that line. Attributes are NOT similarly distinguished: every Group/Unit/Segment/XliffFile.attributes dict holds both standard and vendor-custom attributes together with no marker for which is which.

2. Scoped the build honestly around that finding rather than inventing a new modeled/unmodeled split: CANONICAL mode drops every ExtensionNode at every tree level; every attributes dict entry is preserved in both modes. Documented this explicitly in the new module's own docstring, matching this session's established GAP-008 practice (ipynb execution adapter, nrrd lazy payload access).

3. Built codec/preservation.py as a new, purely additive module: PreservationMode (StrEnum: LOSSLESS/CANONICAL, mirroring safetensors' PayloadAccessMode naming convention), LossReport (frozen slotted dataclass: is_lossless, dropped_count, dropped_tags, detail), canonicalize() (walks the tree via four small per-level helpers mirroring writer.py's own _write_segment/_write_unit/_write_group/_write_file structure, returns a new document with every ExtensionNode dropped plus the dropped tags in document order -- uses dataclasses.replace() so the original document's children lists are never mutated), and check_preservation() (calls canonicalize() and reports what it found, without serializing).

4. Threaded a keyword-only mode: PreservationMode = PreservationMode.LOSSLESS parameter through the actual exported codec/writer/writer.py dumps()/dump() (not a parallel unused API) -- LOSSLESS is a no-op preserving this function's exact historical behavior; CANONICAL calls canonicalize() before the existing serialization logic runs, unchanged otherwise. This directly satisfies the obligation's literal text ('dumps()/dump() take no preservation-mode parameter').

5. Smoke-tested manually before writing formal tests: built a document with extensions at every tree level, confirmed check_preservation() reports all four dropped tags, confirmed CANONICAL output omits them while LOSSLESS output contains them, confirmed the default (no mode= passed) equals explicit LOSSLESS, confirmed canonicalize() does not mutate the original document (list lengths on the source document unchanged after the call), confirmed a clean document with no extensions produces byte-identical LOSSLESS and CANONICAL output.

6. Caught one real correctness bug during smoke-testing, not by mypy or tests: writer.py's mode-validation branch used `mode is PreservationMode.CANONICAL` (identity comparison). Since PreservationMode is a StrEnum, a caller passing the plain string 'canonical' (equal by value, not identity) would incorrectly hit the 'unknown mode' error branch. Fixed by switching to `==`/`!=`, then added test_plain_string_matching_enum_value_is_accepted to lock the correct behavior in.
7. Ran ruff and mypy on all four changed/new files: both clean on the first pass after step 6's fix.

8. Wrote test_obligation_preservation_mode.py (18 tests): default-mode identity, LOSSLESS preserving every extension level, LOSSLESS dump/load roundtrip, unknown-mode rejection (both enum and plain-string paths), CANONICAL dropping every tree level including segment-level extensions, CANONICAL output still loading cleanly, CANONICAL as a no-op on extension-free documents, CANONICAL preserving all attributes (the documented scope boundary), canonicalize() not mutating the original document, canonicalize() returning tags in document order, check_preservation() on clean and lossy documents, check_preservation() matching canonicalize()'s drop count, and two tests against documents produced by the real loads() reader (not just hand-built fixtures) to prove the report works on genuinely parsed XML, not only synthetic dataclass trees.

9. One own-test bug found and fixed during the first run: test_canonical_mode_drops_segment_level_extension asserted the LOSSLESS output contained the tag name exactly once, but an XML element's tag legitimately appears twice (open and close tags) -- fixed the assertion to check presence, not count.

10. Ran the full xliff suite: 313 passed (295 baseline + 18 new), 0 regressions. Promoted both XLIFF-PRESERVE-001 obligations to implemented -- the third genuinely new (not citation-corrected) capability closure this session, after the ipynb execution adapter and nrrd lazy payload access.
